verdict.rationale: First-party docs state Linux machines can be created from the console, REST API, or CLI, with GPU and multi-GPU machine types selectable at creation. An 'ML in a Box' template comes preinstalled with ML frameworks and CUDA drivers, and SSH with root access is supported. A community user confirms running personal ML projects on a Paperspace GPU VM, but another reported SSH access was an uphill battle, and high-end GPUs such as the H100 require approval before use. Missing for 10: independent evidence of actual time-to-running-code (the 'seconds' claim is marketing only), immediate on-demand access to high-end GPUs without an approval gate, and a published API spec for programmatic provisioning (OpenAPI probe returned 404).
